learning.title: A test stack's first boot may repeat only after the named host-port bind collision
learning.trigger: compose up fails with RootlessKit PortManager.AddPort(): listen tcp4 127.0.0.1:PORT: bind: address already in use.
learning.mistake: Stack setups drew ports with a listen on port 0 that they closed before compose bound them, and Docker's own port 0 choice lost to a host socket outside its bookkeeping (inngest on 127.0.0.1:33306, PR 537 dispatch). No allocator can exclude such a socket, and the setups retried unevenly: the durable-core stack once on its first boot, the skill-import stack and two materialize-authorized-skills-worker tests through bindLoopbackPortWithRetry, the rest not at all.
learning.rule: Boot through retryOnPortCollision (tests/fixtures/loopback-port-allocation.ts): draw ports inside run so every attempt re-draws, and on exactly that error clean the project the attempt owns, restore its owned networks and boot again, at most three times, announcing each lost race on stderr as [port-collision-retry] so a boot that needed one says so. Any other error rethrows at once with no cleanup. A first boot cleans the project it owns. A restart of a pinned port (the durable-core engine, stopped and started again) must not clean: it has nothing to remove (the failed up leaves a created container that the next up recreates), so it passes a no-op cleanup, re-draws the port, updates the port its consumers read (stack.ports.inngest) and starts again; CI run 42870736271 lost 127.0.0.1:33604 that way while the engine was stopped.

verification.requirement: tests/unit/loopback-port-allocation_test.ts covers the exact CI text, a non-matching error, exhaustion, a first-attempt success and the announcement of each lost race (none for an unrelated error).
